title: Error with Color Picker in CAD Sfotware

judgment.rationale: The workspace/menu split is a focused capture-path regression candidate, not an activation or color-format settings problem. Compare the sampled desktop surface against the visible CAD viewport before blaming ZWCAD's renderer or replacing the capture backend. Existing screenshot and software/version details are enough for a maintainer test; do not request them again.
evidence: The author supplies ZWCAD 2026 on Windows 10 22H2, PowerToys 0.102.2933, an example screenshot and a diagnostic ZIP.
Both Model Space and Paper Space are affected; menus are a working control. The author says a prior PowerToys version sampled the workspace correctly.
The screenshot was visually inspected: the picker displays 50,50,50 over visibly different drawing content. The Color Picker module log records activations, not a graphics-capture failure stack.

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Mouse/MouseInfoProvider.cs: Current sampling uses a cached one-pixel GDI surface and Graphics.CopyFromScreen with SourceCopy, then reads that pixel; capture failure can preserve the previous color. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI/Mouse/MouseInfoProvider.cs
Downloaded and visually inspected the CAD screenshot; downloaded the report and read Color Picker module/application excerpts. No supplied trace proves a GPU-overlay, DPI, or cached-color mechanism.
Reviewed the current sampling implementation and bounded Color Picker PR/history results; #49174 migrated the UI/sampling implementation but does not establish a ZWCAD workspace fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare ZWCAD viewport pixels with the GDI sample

fix_assessment.rationale: Qualified lightweight investigation/fix direction, not a full design. The screenshot and menu/workspace control isolate the symptom well, but no raw capture outcome or rendering comparison identifies surface mismatch versus failed/stale sample.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve the CAD viewport's captured-surface or stale-sample mismatch
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis only: the GDI sample sees a different composited surface or retains a previous color after failure; the screenshot proves the wrong result, not which mechanism caused it.
plan: Reproduce the existing Model/Paper/menu control matrix and compare visible desktop pixels with successful/raw capture and cached-color state.
If capture fails, correct/report the recoverable sample state; if the desktop surface differs, evaluate a bounded compatible capture fallback rather than changing output format.
Retain the non-sensitive drawing/color fixture and test coordinate, DPI, menu, multi-monitor and ordinary-app controls.
verification: Differently colored CAD workspace pixels no longer all return 50,50,50.
Menus and ordinary applications remain correct, capture failure does not silently masquerade as a valid stale color, and sampling stays responsive.

confidence.rationale: The screenshot and menu/workspace control isolate the symptom well, but no raw capture outcome or rendering comparison identifies surface mismatch versus failed/stale sample.

information_gaps.information: Raw sampled pixel/capture outcome versus visible workspace and cached color
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguish a graphics-surface mismatch from recoverable capture failure or stale state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer should run the supplied ZWCAD setup and compare raw GDI result/exception, cached color and same-coordinate desktop screenshot before selecting a backend change.

actions.label: Compare ZWCAD viewport pixels with the GDI sample

reproduce.title: Compare ZWCAD viewport pixels with the GDI sample
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.102.2933 versus current stable/main; ZWCAD 2026 on Windows 10 22H2.
prerequisites: Use an isolated test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: 1. Open a non-sensitive drawing with several clearly different solid colors in Model Space and Paper Space; keep menus as a working control.
2. Activate the picker and compare expected visible pixel colors with sampled values at the same screen coordinates.
3. Capture a desktop screenshot of the same pixels and, in a maintainer diagnostic session, compare raw CopyFromScreen return/color, exception outcome, and last cached color.
4. Only if the workspace differs at that capture boundary, compare a supported alternate desktop-capture path or controlled CAD rendering option; preserve coordinate/DPI mapping.
reproduce.expected_result: Workspace and menu pixels match their visible colors, or the failing graphics boundary is specifically identified without changing the app's drawing data.
